_comment: preview.coo.ee's PUBLISHED CATALOG SET — deployment config for one specific box, NOT image content. Kept out of deploy/image/ deliberately: baking it there made every adopter of the prebuilt image open on these catalogs (see the seed's comment). Changes on main are applied directly by publish-preview-config.yml; image publishes reconcile the same file as a fallback. Both paths use .github/scripts/publish-config-to-box.sh additively over POST /admin/catalogs, so this never needs an image rebuild. Another deployment adopting the preview server keeps its own copy of this shape and points DEPLOY_CONFIG_DIR at it. Every entry's design-artifacts/<system> branch must be trusted by producers.json beside this file. cadence is listed:false — reachable at /cadence/ but off the front-page index. compose-m3 and wear-m3 are listed:false for the same reason from the other direction: they are compose-ai-tools' own in-repo harness catalogs — they exist to exercise the preview pipeline's features, not to be a design system. m3-catalog is the real Material 3 reference and wear-m3-catalog will be the Wear one, so the two harness catalogs stay reachable at /compose-m3/ and /wear-m3/ as a live smoke target without presenting as design systems on the front page. loadPriority (default 0, highest first) is the startup FETCH order and nothing else — the list order above still decides the front page. A group's priority (default 0, highest first) is the FRONT-PAGE SECTION order: design-systems sits at 100 so the two reference design systems head the page however late their catalogs register, since a catalog published through the admin API is appended and used to drag its whole section to the bottom (#4601). Within a section the catalog list order still decides the cards. m3-catalog and wear-m3-catalog are the two reference design systems this box exists to serve, and being published late left them last in the queue (a runtime registration is appended), so a rollout served everything else first; they now lead it (#4231). NOTE the reconcile is additive (see publish-config-to-box.sh): it never deletes. Re-posting an entry whose listed, group or loadPriority changed converges it in place; an otherwise-unchanged one comes back 409. repo is the one field a re-post cannot converge — the server refuses to re-point a catalog under an existing id — so publish-config-to-box.sh reads GET /admin/catalogs first and, where the live repo differs from the one declared here, retires that id (DELETE /admin/catalogs/<system>) immediately before the POST re-creates it. That is what re-points a catalog that changed repositories, remote-m3 -> yschimke/wear-m3-catalog (#4588) being the case it was written for; without it the 409 reads as success while the box goes on serving the old repository's frozen branch. An unchanged catalog is never retired, and a box whose listing cannot be read degrades to the additive behaviour rather than failing the publish (both pinned in test-publish-config-to-box.sh). producers.json beside this file must still trust the new repo's design-artifacts/*, or the re-pointed catalog serves as `unverified`.
_sites_comment: TOP-LEVEL SITES — a catalog above, additionally served on a hostname of its own where it presents as the only thing on the box: landing at /, links inside the domain, no front door, /status + /sitemap.xml scoped to it, /<other-system>/ 404. Same sessions and same baked pixels as the canonical /<system>/ path, so a site adds no catalog, no daemon and no render. Two prerequisites OUTSIDE this file: DNS for the name must point at the box, and Caddy must route it here with a certificate. Delivered by the SAME additive reconcile as the catalogs (publish-config-to-box.sh POSTs each entry to /admin/sites, after the catalogs loop because a site may only name a catalog the box already serves), so a hostname committed here reaches the running box on the next push to main. It used to reach nothing: this file is read at startup and seeded onto its volume once, so a site had to be spelled a second time in SERVE_SITES in the box's untracked .env. The EDGE half is derived from this same list by the caddy container (deploy/image/caddy-entrypoint.sh), which reads it when Caddy starts — so a site added here is served by the app as soon as the reconcile runs, and reachable over TLS after the next `docker compose up -d`.
